title: Oily Dutch Poffertjes Pancake
description: A spicy, shattering, and nostalgic Dutch dish featuring nutmeg and bonito-shave that's perfect for ayurvedic-tamasic-friendly diets.
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, and yeast in a large mixing bowl.
Heat milk, melted butter, buttermilk, and vegetable oil in a saucepan until warm, around 100°F (38°C).
Whisk in eggs and cayenne pepper, then slowly pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let the mixture rest in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
Preheat a non-stick pan or a poffertjes pan over medium heat with a small amount of vegetable oil.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop the batter into the pan and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and puffed up.
Repeat with the remaining batter, greasing the pan with more oil as needed.
Serve warm with a sprinkle of bonito flakes and a pinch of nutmeg.
These poffertjes are best served immediately, but they can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 hours.
Note: Traditionally, poffertjes are cooked in a special poffertjes pan that has many small cups. If you have access to one, use it!
If not, a non-stick pan will do the job just fine.
Poffertjes are best served with butter and powdered sugar, but feel free to get creative with toppings!
